- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts too high; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.53) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; cap upward revisions at +3% of recent mean to prevent runaway growth.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.27–0.53), model shows lag in adjusting to true trend; delay forecast update by 1–2 days if sentiment shifts sharply.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 3σ from 30-day moving average, model tends to overpredict; apply downward correction proportional to deviation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes (last 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 forecast points if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
